jobs.prompt:
AIPass @daemon WEEKLY wake for @seedgo - the v5 shadow cadence. Do ONLY this, nothing else.
1. From the repo root run: drone @seedgo shadow-cycle run
   Measured: about 2 minutes on a warm audit cache and about 6 minutes on a cold one (the fleet pytest_quality pass is the long pole), and longer on a slower host. Start it in the BACKGROUND and poll until it exits - a foreground bash call is capped at 10 minutes and would be killed mid-audit.
2. The verb emails its own one-screen summary to @devpulse. Do not send any other mail.
3. Report the three headline numbers it printed - the pytest_quality shadow average, the test-function count, the consolidation-candidate count - then STOP.
Do NOT run startup, do NOT update memories, do NOT open or close plans, do NOT fix anything, and do NOT act on any number it prints: the pytest_quality pack is SHADOW and gates nothing. If the verb fails, report the error verbatim and STOP.
jobs._slot: Intended slot: Sunday 03:00 local. An interval job has no time field - it fires on the first daemon tick after it is enabled and then every 10080 minutes from that moment, so the slot is set by SEEDING last_run, not by this file (drone @daemon run --help: 'No native offset field. Seed different last_run values in daemon_json/daemon_runstate.json'). Sunday 03:00 is the quiet window: no human at the keyboard, no PR train, and clear of @daemon's own 09:00 inbox-sweep. The cycle saturates the CPU for its whole run (pyright per branch, one git blame per test file) and it evicts the aipass-pack audit cache, so the next interactive 'audit aipass' is a cold full scan - both are reasons it must not land during a working session.
jobs._note: ENABLED 2026-09-07 01:39 on Patrick's ruling (01:16, relayed by devpulse in FPLAN-0491: seal DPLAN-0323, switch the weekly v5 cadence on). SLOT SEEDED by @daemon at 01:48 the same night: daemon_json/daemon_runstate.json now carries last_run 2026-09-06T03:00:00 and next_run 2026-09-13T03:00:00, so the 10080-minute week counts from Sunday 03:00 as intended. @daemon verified it against is_job_due() at six instants rather than by eye; the Sunday 03:00 boundary is exact because interval measures from last_run, not from last success. WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED IN BETWEEN, recorded because it was luck and not a guard: the job tried to fire TWICE before the seed landed - @daemon's logs/run.log lines 61-62, 01:34:52 and 01:40:20, both 'Blocked firing @seedgo/shadow-cycle-weekly: lock: Active agent (PID 432478)'. The only thing that stopped the week locking to 01:34 Monday was that seedgo happened to be awake in its own branch holding that lock. record_job_blocked leaves last_run alone on purpose, so _is_interval_due kept answering True on every tick and the sole brake was _in_blocked_hold's five minutes. The ordering in the line below is therefore not advice, it is the measured consequence of getting it wrong: SEED FIRST, THEN ENABLE.
